Messages.Author: Xaddam
Messages.Body:
I'm wondering about the interaction between Mirror Walk and the slave rule. If an action is blocked with a Mirror Walk played can the acting minion's methuselah use the slave rule to untap the acting minion and have a gargoyle start a combat with the blocking minion?

I'd argue no because the action ends at the time the action is blocked.
I'd argue yes because (in some cases) you're allowed to choose the order in which to resolve your own effects (end action vs. slave rule in this case).
Which one is correct and why?

Thanks in advance.

Slave: Some minions are identified as slaves to a specified clan. A slave cannot take a directed action if his controller doesn�t control a ready member of the specified clan. Also, if a member of the specified clan controlled by the same Methuselah is blocked, the controller can tap the slave to cancel the combat and to untap the acting vampire and have the slave enter combat with the blocking minion instead.

Mirror Walk [Third:C, KoT:C]
Cardtype: Action Modifier
Discipline: Thaumaturgy
Do not replace until your discard phase.
[tha] +1 stealth.
[THA] As [tha] above, and if this action is blocked, the action ends (with no combat).

Adam Esbjörnsson,
Prince of Örebro

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Xaddam wrote:
> I'm wondering about the interaction between Mirror Walk and the slave rule. If an action is blocked with a Mirror Walk played can the acting minion's methuselah use the slave rule to untap the acting minion and have a gargoyle start a combat with the blocking minion?
>
Assuming superior Mirror Walk: no.

> Xaddam wrote:
> I'd argue no because the action ends at the time the action is blocked.
> I'd argue yes because (in some cases) you're allowed to choose the order in which to resolve your own effects (end action vs. slave rule in this case).
> Which one is correct and why?
>
The latter, due to the "instead" word in the Slave rule. If the acting vampire isn't entering combat, the Slave can't step in for him.

Messages.Author: Forhead
Messages.Body:
I got a similar question concerning the Slave rule and Stone travel.

1) Is the same true for stone travel? (since there is not "end action" text)
2) Is it possible for the salve to use the "choose to cancel the resultning combat"?

Stone Travel
Type: Action Modifier
Requires: Mytherceria/Obtenebration
[obt] This vampire burns 1 blood to get +1 stealth.
[myt] +1 stealth.
[MYT] +1 stealth. If this action is blocked, this acting vampire may choose to cancel the resulting combat.

Isak Esbjörnsson Bjärmark

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Forhead wrote:
> I got a similar question concerning the Slave rule and Stone travel.
>
> 1) Is the same true for stone travel? (since there is not "end action" text)
>
I'm not sure what "the same" is, but if a vampire is blocked after playing sup'Stone Travel, a Slave to that vampire's clan can't step in for a combat that was cancelled.

> Forhead wrote:
> 2) Is it possible for the salve to use the "choose to cancel the resultning combat"?
>
No - the Slave mininon stepping in doesn't become the acting minion: the Slave can't play Freak Drive, As the Crow, Momentery Delay, ..

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body: Well Stone Travel gives you option to cancel the combat, you don't -have- to cancel it like you do for Mirror Walk.

Messages.Body:

> I got a similar question concerning the Slave rule and Stone travel.

IANF, but anything that cancels the resulting combat of a blocked action, ends the action if it doesn't add anything else to do.
So, if the Stone Traveler chooses to cancel combat, he cannot trigger the Slave Rule.
If he chooses not to cancel the resulting combat and has a ready Slave that meets the requirements, the player can use the Slave Rule.

Right, mr. Floppy?

Messages.Body:
> Brum wrote:
>
> > Forhead wrote:

> > Requires: Mytherceria/Obtenebration
> > [obt] This vampire burns 1 blood to get +1 stealth.
> > [myt] +1 stealth.
> > [MYT] +1 stealth. If this action is blocked, this acting vampire may choose to cancel the resulting combat.
> >
> IANF, but anything that cancels the resulting combat of a blocked action, ends the action if it doesn't add anything else to do.
> So, if the Stone Traveler chooses to cancel combat, he cannot trigger the Slave Rule.
> If he chooses not to cancel the resulting combat and has a ready Slave that meets the requirements, the player can use the Slave Rule.
>
> Right, mr. Floppy?
>
> EDIT: I started writing this before there where answers
>
Cancelling combat doesn't end the action. Your vampire playing sup' Stone Travel can still play sup' Freak Drive or Momentary Delay. The blocking minion can play Cats' Guidance.

If you cancel the resulting combat, you can't invoke the Slave rule.
If you invoke the Slave rule, the generated combat isn't the combat resulting of the block, so you can't choose to cancel it.
So, with sup' Stone Travel, it's one of
- have resulting combat
- cancel resulting combat
- invoke the Slave rule
and then, unless the action somehow continues (Momentary Delay, mostly, I guess), the end of the action is reached for good.

The way I see it, canceling a combat resulting from a block is an effect, not a prerequisite for invoking the slave rule in the same way that untapping the target is an effect, not a prerequisite for Precognizant Mobility. The effect is applied but there is no actual state change, so Vampiric Disease doesn't trigger and the Gargoyle gets in to combat.

As for question #4, I don't see any contradiction. The acting vampire doesn't cancel the combat that isn't coming, the blocking vampire gets to diablerize as normal.
